title: PROlog survey definition
description:
Declarative definition of one survey version: sections, ordered questions, options, per-type config, visibility rules, presentation and participation settings. One file per (survey, version). The runner renders it; the backend stores it verbatim as the immutable SurveyVersion definition. Schema version 1.

The survey is a directed acyclic graph (DAG): questions are nodes; every `visible_if` condition and every `rows_from` reference is a directed edge from the dependent question (or section) to the question it depends on. The graph is acyclic by construction: an edge may only point to a question that appears EARLIER in presentation order (sections in array order, then questions in array order), so the presentation order is a topological order and visibility can be evaluated in a single forward pass. JSON Schema cannot express this ordering rule; the semantic validator (`validate_definition`) enforces it and rejects forward references, self-references and cycles.

schema_version.description: Definition format version this file targets. Omitted = 1.

version.description: Version of this survey's content. New wording or structure = new version; responses stay bound to the version they answered.

translation_status.description: Per non-default language: machine = machine-translated placeholder (must not be published), reviewed = approved by the survey owner's translators. A language without an entry is treated as reviewed only if it is the default language.

intro.description: Participant-facing welcome text shown on the intro page.

completion.description: Participant-facing text shown on the completion page after submission.

theme.description: Theme code resolved by the deployment (see theme.schema.json). Unknown or omitted = the runner's default theme.

i18n.description: Localized text keyed by language code. The survey's default_language key is required; missing languages fall back to it.

participation.description: Who may respond and how a respondent is identified.

anonymous.description: true = respondents need no account; the response id held by the browser is the only credential. false (default) = respondents must be authenticated by the host platform.

resume.description: How an in-progress response is resumed. browser_token (default for anonymous) = response id kept in browser storage; account = attached to the authenticated user; none = no resume.

repeat.description: Optional repeat administration for invited (non-anonymous) participants.

use_current_version.description: true = each administration uses the then-published version; false (default) = the version scheduled.

presentation.description: How the runner lays the instrument out. Defaults reproduce a one-question-per-screen wizard.

mode.description: question (default) = one question per screen. "section" (one section per screen) is reserved for a later phase: it is accepted structurally but rejected by the semantic validator until the runner implements it.

overview.description: Show the 'all questions' overview that lets a respondent jump back to any reachable question. Default true.

section_interstitials.description: Show a lightweight, data-free interstitial when entering a new section. Default true.

skip_policy.description: Applies to questions with required=true. soft (default) = one-time 'skip this question?' confirmation, then an explicit skip is recorded; hard = cannot advance unanswered; none = silent skip.

consent.description: Versioned consent attestation shown before the first question. Recorded as an attestation, never as an answer.

required.description: true (default) = the respondent must actively agree before starting.

visible_if.description: All conditions must hold (AND) for the whole section to be shown. DAG rule: each condition may reference only a question in an EARLIER section.

questions.description: Presentation order within the section; sections themselves run in array order.

key.description: Globally unique within the survey; answer records reference it.

type.description: info = read-only text block (no answer). single/dropdown = one option. multi = many options. scale = one integer on a labelled scale. ranking = ordered options. matrix = one scale value per row. text/number/date/email = typed input.

required.description: true (default) = subject to the survey's skip_policy. false = plainly optional, no nudge. Ignored for info.

visible_if.description: All conditions must hold (AND) for the question to be shown. Hiding a question invalidates its stored answer. DAG rule: each condition may reference only a question that appears EARLIER in presentation order (never itself, never a later question).

exclusive.description: Selecting this option clears all others in a multi-select (e.g. "I am not sure").

free_text.description: Selecting this option reveals an inline text input stored as other_text (e.g. "Other (free text)").

op.description: eq/neq: single-valued answer equals / does not equal value. in: single-valued answer is one of values. contains: multi-valued answer includes value. answered: question has a non-skipped answer. `question` is a DAG edge and must point to an earlier question.

min_selections.description: multi: minimum picks for the answer to count as answered (default 1).

options_source.description: dropdown: named built-in option list provided by the runner (inline options, if present, are appended after it).

point_labels.description: One label per point, min..max (used by matrix legends and labelled scales).

rows_from.description: matrix: question key whose selected option keys become this question's rows (dynamic rows). DAG rule: must be a `multi` question that appears EARLIER in presentation order.

optional_items.description: ranking: option keys the respondent may leave out of the ranking (e.g. "other").

multiline.description: text: render a multi-line textarea (default true when max_length > 200).

min_date.description: date: inclusive lower bound, ISO 8601 date.

max_date.description: date: inclusive upper bound, ISO 8601 date.

store_separately.description: email: contact capture. The address is persisted in a separate contact table with no link to the response, and is never returned by the API or included in answer exports.

link_identity.description: email: identity capture. The address is sent to the host platform's identity service, which creates or finds a participant record; the response is linked to that record. Mutually exclusive with store_separately. Requires the integrated deployment profile.
